question: A 39-year-old woman presents to your office with 4 days of fever, sore throat, generalized aching, arthralgias, and tender nodules on both of her shins that arose in the last 48 hours. Her medical history is negative for disease and she does not take oral contraceptives or any other medication regularly. The physical examination reveals the vital signs that include body temperature 38.5°C (101.3°F), heart rate 85/min, blood pressure 120/65 mm Hg, tender and enlarged submandibular lymph nodes, and an erythematous, edematous, and swollen pharynx with enlarged tonsils and a patchy white exudate on the surface. She is not pregnant. Examination of the lower limbs reveals erythematous, tender, immobile nodules on both shins. You do not identify ulcers or similar lesions on other areas of her body. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Streptococcal pharyngitis -> immune complex deposition in skin -> erythema nodosum -> 80% CHAIN: Streptococcal infection -> inflammatory response -> tender nodules on shins -> erythema nodosum -> 75% CHAIN: Streptococcal infection -> cytokine release -> skin inflammation -> erythema nodosum -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis in this patient is Erythema nodosum. Streptococcal infection can lead to an inflammatory response causing tender nodules on the shins, which aligns with the presentation of erythema nodosum in this case. Evidence paths support the association between streptococcal infections and the development of erythema nodosum through immune complex deposition and skin inflammation.
analysis: The patient's presentation of fever, sore throat, arthralgias, and tender nodules on both shins, along with the absence of ulcers or similar lesions, is highly suggestive of erythema nodosum. The presence of streptococcal infection further supports this diagnosis, as streptococcal infections are known triggers for erythema nodosum. The physical exam findings of tender and enlarged submandibular lymph nodes, along with an erythematous, edematous, and swollen pharynx with enlarged tonsils, are consistent with a streptococcal infection. Erythema nodosum is a type of panniculitis characterized by tender, erythematous nodules on the shins, often associated with systemic conditions like infections. The absence of other specific symptoms or history pointing to alternative diagnoses makes erythema nodosum the most likely diagnosis in this case.
